description: If the current app is available, use its json.dumps method; otherwise, use json.dumps from the json module.
If the current app is available, use its json.dump method; otherwise, use json.dump from the json module.
If the current app is available, use its json.loads method; otherwise, use json.loads from the json module.
If the current app is available, use its json.load method; otherwise, use json.load from the json module.
Serialize the given arguments as JSON and return a flask.Response object with the application/json mimetype; it requires an active app context.
The application must have a `static_folder` set to serve static files.
The application can only be run using `app.run()` if it is not invoked from Flask's command line interface.
The configuration of `SERVER_NAME` must be set to enable subdomain routing and must not rely on default values.
The return value of request handlers must be a valid response type (string, bytes, dict, list, tuple, or response object).
If `max_age` is set to None, the browser should use conditional requests instead of a timed cache.
If any `before_request` handler returns a non-None value, request handling must stop immediately.
All exceptions raised by view functions will not be propagated if `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` is False and not in debug mode.
View functions must not return None, strings, or unrecognized types as response objects.
When in debug mode, Flask will show the full stack trace of exceptions occurred during a request.
The application must load the nearest `'.env'` and `'.flaskenv'` files to set environment variables when `load_dotenv` is set to True.
The application requires that `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY` is set to True.
The application will serve a static file only if `static_folder` is defined and set properly.
All request teardown functions will be called regardless of whether an exception was raised during the request.
Errors during the request teardown are collected and must be raised if they occur.
The application must raise an error if `make_response` receives an invalid response type from a view function.
URLs generated through `url_for` may include an anchor if provided as `_anchor` argument.
The application should provide automatic options responses if `provide_automatic_options` is True and the request method is OPTIONS.
The application must check whether the `static_host` and `host_matching` are consistent when adding a static route.
The 'static_folder' must be set to serve static files.
Resources can only be opened for reading.
The default configuration for SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT is None, which tells the browser to use conditional requests instead of a timed cache.
If SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT is set, it should be returned in seconds; otherwise, None should be returned.
Only 'r', 'rt', and 'rb' are valid modes for opening a resource file.
A Flask application must be specified using the '--app' option, 'FLASK_APP' environment variable, or a 'wsgi.py' or 'app.py' file in the current directory.
If multiple Flask applications are detected in a module, a NoAppException will be raised, requiring specification of the correct one.
A factory function for creating a Flask application must be callable without arguments, otherwise a NoAppException is raised.
If the specified application name is not a valid attribute name or a valid function call, a NoAppException will be raised.
The environment variable FLASK_DEBUG controls whether the application runs in debug mode.
If the debug option is not explicitly set, it defaults to the value of the FLASK_DEBUG environment variable.
The command to launch the development server ('run') should only be used for development purposes and is not suitable for production.
The command 'routes' shows all registered routes in the application along with their associated methods and endpoints.
A command will always run within the context of the application's app context using the decorator 'with_appcontext'.
When using SSL, if '--key' is provided, '--cert' must also be specified.
The application context for commands must be loaded unless already active, and must be preserved across command invocations.
If an error occurs while loading the application, the error will propagate immediately unless it's a reloading scenario, in which case the error will display without stopping the server.
The application must be initialized before executing any server commands.
The loading of environment variables from '.env' or '.flaskenv' files is governed by the 'load_dotenv_defaults' parameter, which defaults to True.
The 'after_this_request' function can only be used when a request context is active, such as in a view function.
The 'copy_current_request_context' function can only be used when a request context is active, such as in a view function.
The 'request' property of AppContext raises a RuntimeError if the context does not have an associated request.
The 'session' property of AppContext raises a RuntimeError if the context does not have an associated request.
The push method of AppContext can trigger request matching only if the context is not already pushed.
The pop method of AppContext raises a RuntimeError if it is not the active context or if it has been pushed more times than it has been popped.
If a request context is active, the has_request_context function returns True; otherwise, it returns False.
If an app context is active, the has_app_context function returns True; otherwise, it returns False.
The AppContext constructor initializes the app context and sets the request and session to None if not provided.
The session is loaded the first time it is accessed, rather than when the context is pushed.
Teardown functions are evaluated when the context is popped, depending on whether the context is a request or an app context.
A JSONProvider must implement the dumps and loads methods for serialization and deserialization.
Either positional or keyword arguments can be given to the response method, but not both.
If no arguments are given to the response method, None is serialized.
Response output is in 'application/json' mimetype.
The response method serializes the given arguments as JSON before returning the response.
The dumps method must sort keys in any serialized dictionaries if sort_keys is set to True.
The default method must return a valid JSON type or raise a TypeError if serialization fails.
The loads method must deserialize data from a string or bytes as JSON.
The compact attribute controls the formatting of the response output based on its value and debugging mode.
The ensure_ascii attribute determines if non-ASCII characters are replaced with escape sequences during JSON serialization.
The dumps method must apply default serialization behaviors defined in the attributes of the JSONProvider.
A file must be opened for writing with UTF-8 encoding to write valid JSON using the dump method.
The load method deserializes data read from a file that is opened for reading text or UTF-8 bytes.
If data is of type date, it will be serialized to HTTP date format using the default method.
UUID and decimal types are serialized to strings using the default function during JSON serialization.
Dataclasses are converted to dictionaries using dataclasses.asdict during serialization.
A session is permanent if the '_permanent' key is set to True.
A session is marked as new if it is created for the first time, although this is not guaranteed.
The modified flag for a session must be set to True when data in the session is changed.
The accessed flag indicates if the session has been accessed even if it was not modified.
If a session is modified or is permanent with SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST set to True, a Set-Cookie header should be set for the session cookie.
A null session will be generated if the open_session method fails or returns None.
The name of the session cookie is obtained from app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_NAME'].
The domain for the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN'].
The path for the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_PATH'] or falls back to app.config['APPLICATION_ROOT'].
The httponly status of the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY'].
The secure status of the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE'].
The SameSite attribute for the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE'].
The partitioned status of the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED'].
The expiration time of the session is calculated based on whether the session is permanent and the app's permanent_session_lifetime.
If the session is empty and modified, the cookie should be deleted from the response.
If a cookie should be set for the session, it can only be done if the session is not empty and either modified or allowed to be refreshed.
Signals are created for various stages of a Flask application lifecycle.
The signal 'template-rendered' is used to indicate that a template has been rendered.
The signal 'before-render-template' is used to indicate that a template is about to be rendered.
The signal 'request-started' is used to indicate that a request has started processing.
The signal 'request-finished' is used to indicate that a request has finished processing.
The signal 'request-tearing-down' is used to indicate that a request context is being torn down.
The signal 'got-request-exception' is used to indicate that an exception occurred during request processing.
The signal 'appcontext-tearing-down' is used to indicate that the application context is being torn down.
The signal 'appcontext-pushed' is used to indicate that the application context is being pushed onto the stack.
The signal 'appcontext-popped' is used to indicate that the application context is being popped from the stack.
The signal 'message-flashed' is used to indicate that a message has been flashed to the user.
The base_url must be either absent or should not coexist with subdomain or url_scheme.
The base_url must not be passed together with subdomain or url_scheme.
If base_url is None, it will be constructed from the server name and application root.
If subdomain is provided, it will prepend the server name.
If url_scheme is None, it will default to the application's preferred URL scheme.
The REMOTE_ADDR in environments base is set to '127.0.0.1'.
The HTTP_USER_AGENT in environments base is set to Werkzeug version string.
A session transaction can be initiated using a with statement.
Cookies must be enabled for session transactions to proceed.
If the session backend does not open a session, a RuntimeError is raised.
The invoke method for the FlaskCliRunner defaults to the application's CLI group if no CLI command is provided.
If 'obj' is not provided in kwargs for invoking a CLI command, a ScriptInfo instance will be passed.
